title: In Silico review provenance
$comment: Two record shapes share this file. Version 2 is the hosted panel: five referees, two audits, a debate, and a dollar cost. Version 4 is a review generated locally by the plugin that ships inside peerreviewagents 0.9, which runs every agent inside one Claude Code session on a subscription, where most of the panel's numbers do not exist and inventing zeros for them would read as measurements. Version 3 was the shape the engine's own Python orchestration wrote on the same subscription. That orchestration is deleted in 0.9 with no shim, and no version 3 record was ever published, so its shape is gone from this file rather than left selectable: a schema that still accepted it would let a record claim a single requested model and a publish-time login probe that nothing in the repository can now produce. Fields common to both shapes are required here, and each version's own obligations are in allOf below. Records written before versioning carry no schema_version and are not validated at all, so nothing already published has to be rewritten.

generator.$comment: Required on a version 4 record, and present on no other shape. It answers who ran this review, on what code, through which billing route, with which agents, and whether a person read it before it was published. The engine and plugin fingerprints are over the source trees the run itself recorded, so two reviews claiming the same release can be shown to have run the same bytes.

engine.$comment: The installed distribution. 0.9 exposes no module version and no API version of its own, so there is one source for this and a record that cannot name it is refused rather than written with an empty string.

engine_fingerprint.$comment: source names where the hashed manifest came from. run_manifest is the engine's own record of every file it loaded at the moment the run started, which is the only one that describes the code that wrote the review. installed_engine is a re-hash of whatever is installed on the publishing machine, which is a different claim. matches_installed_engine is present when both could be compared.

plugin.$comment: The plugin is what reviews the paper in 0.9, so the record names it by its bytes rather than by its version. Two runs can both say plugin-two-track-v1 over different agent prompts, and the fingerprint settles which ran. workflow_sha256 is the hash of the one file that decides which agents run in what order. matches_installed_plugin is present when the plugin installed on the publishing machine could be hashed and compared.

transport.$comment: paid_api_key_used is a const rather than a boolean. A record that needs to say true is not a local subscription run and does not belong in this shape. The claim the block makes is deliberately narrow: not that an account of a particular kind paid, since 0.9 reads no authentication status and this schema will not hold a guess, but that a real Claude Code session started, loaded the engine's plugin and connected its MCP server, and ran with no API key in its environment.

provider.$comment: In Silico publishes Claude Code runs only. The run records its own transport, and the two are compared before a record is written, so a bundle cannot name one transport over a run that used another. The Codex provider is gone from the engine in 0.9 and gone from here with it.

version.$comment: The Claude Code version the run observed, from runtime.json. Required, because a record that cannot name it did not come from a session that ran.

login_verified.$comment: A const rather than a boolean, for the same reason as paid_api_key_used. A rehearsal written with the check skipped says false here, and a rehearsal is not a published review however it reached this folder.

verified_by.$comment: Where the claim about the transport was read. The run's own start-up probe is the only source: engine 0.9 proves a Claude Code session started, loaded the plugin and connected the peerreview MCP server before it spends anything, and writes that proof into startup.json. The publish-time probe that version 3 used asked the installed CLI who was logged in at the moment the bundle was written, which is a fact about the publishing machine rather than about the review, and 0.9 exposes no authentication status to ask. Nothing published carries either value, so narrowing this rewrote no record.

verified_at.$comment: When the run's probe ran, from startup.json. The run's clock, not the publishing machine's.

agents.$comment: One row per agent that actually ran. The plugin pins a model inside each agent file, so the panel is a list of slots with their own models rather than one requested id repeated down a column, which is what version 3 recorded. A slot the harness reserved and never filled is left out: an agent with no model, no state and no usage reviewed nothing, and five of those would overstate the panel.

input.$comment: The exact bytes the engine read, hashed before the run. A reader who disputes a quotation can fetch the same identifier and compare. local_file says whether those bytes were fetched from the identifier or handed over from the operator's disk, which a reader cannot otherwise tell and which decides whether the hash can be reproduced.

run.$comment: Read through the engine's own reader, never from the prepare step's intentions or the publish flags. What is required here is what a reader needs in order to know how the review was produced and whether it is whole: the arm, the transport, the workflow, the finished state, the engine's publish flag, where the findings came from, the reviewer count and the stage ledger. Everything else is recorded when the run recorded it and left out otherwise, because a value the run never measured must not appear as a default that looks measured. The property list is closed on purpose: the engine's reading also carries `cause` for a run that stopped and `problems` for a run file it could not read in full, and neither can be true of a run it calls publishable, so a bundle carrying one fails here rather than publishing with the explanation of its own failure buried in it.

directory.$comment: Relative to the repository root. An absolute path identifies the machine that wrote the record rather than the review, and this record is published.

arm.$comment: The arm replaces 0.8's mode and review policy, and it is the single name for what the run was asked to do. 0.9 defines full-two-track, reviewers-only, single, single-revision, manuscript-only and draft-check. Left as a string rather than an enum because the engine owns that list, and a record has to be able to name the arm the run actually used rather than one of the arms this repository knew about when it was written.

specialist_tracks.$comment: The audit tracks the arm asked for, as the run's own plan recorded them. The six in 0.9 are stats, figures-tables, methods-reporting, citations, consistency and field. A track listed here with no audit report in the bundle is a gap a reader can see.

status.$comment: The engine writes running, blocked, complete or complete-without-findings, and the last two are its finished states. complete is a review with findings in it. complete-without-findings is a review written with none, which is what the reviewers raising nothing make-or-break looks like, and it publishes: the engine refuses the other run that ends there, the one whose findings the guards all quarantined, and it refuses it on publishable rather than on the status. A bundle written from a run that stopped part way still cannot validate even if its folder is moved into place by hand.

publishable.$comment: The engine's own answer, from read_run, to the only question the publish gate asks: the run finished, the findings came from a readable editor package rather than the ledger, a guard verdict was recorded, the guards did not empty the review, and every run file could be read in full. It is recorded rather than inferred so a reader of the bundle sees the same flag the gate saw, and it is a const because a record written from a run the engine refused has no business on the site.

findings_source.$comment: Where the published findings came from. The editor package is the editor agent's own placement of them. A pool rebuilt from findings.jsonl is the engine's fallback for a run whose editor package is missing or damaged, and it carries no editorial placement at all, so it is not published here.

review_guard_status.$comment: The engine's verdict on its own findings, and it writes exactly two words. clean is a run the guards took nothing from, and quarantined is one they took something from, however much. Both publish: a review that raised nothing is clean with no findings, and one that lost a finding whose quote could not be anchored still endorses the rest, with quarantined_findings_count saying how many were held back. The one run neither word excuses is a review the guards emptied, and the engine refuses that on publishable, naming how many it held.

completeness.$comment: The stage ledger, which is the only thing that says whether the review is whole. The server records the stages the arm requires and the ones that reported, and a run can reach complete with a stage that never reported when the editor agent accepted the pool without it. Publishing refuses a run with anything in missing, so a published record carries an empty list there; the ledger is still written out, because a reader should be able to see it rather than read the absence of a complaint as proof. none_found is the stages that reported nothing to report, which is an answer and not a gap, and retried names the slots that needed more than one attempt.

quarantined_findings_count.$comment: Findings the server refused to accept because they failed the evidence guards. They are counted rather than published, and the count is what tells a reader how much of the review was thrown away before the editor agent saw it.

note.$comment: What the engine records when a review was written and the session was blocked afterwards, by a rate limit or a token ceiling that fired after the review was saved. Such a run is complete and publishable, and the note is the one thing that says the session did not end cleanly, so it is published rather than dropped.

advisory_verdict.$comment: The editor agent's judgement of the manuscript, as it wrote it. 0.9 publishes it rather than discarding it, and it sits here, under the generator and beside decision_source, for a reason: it is the engine's opinion, it is labelled advisory wherever it is shown, and the decision on the record is still a person's. A reader who disagrees with the engine can see its judgement and the editor's decision side by side. An empty object is allowed, because an arm that runs no editor produces no judgement and inventing one would be worse than recording none.

decision_source.$comment: The engine grades findings and offers an advisory judgement. It recommends no accept or reject, so the decision on this record was typed by the editor after reading the run. Recording the engine as its author would be a false attribution.

attestation.$comment: human_reviewed_before_merge stays a const rather than a boolean: this file validates published records, and a record that has to say false is a rehearsal that was never meant to reach the site. editor is required because the generator used to write the attestation as a constant, before any person had acted. An attestation with nobody behind it attests to nothing, so the name of whoever read the run is part of the claim.

rehearsal.$comment: Whether the generator was asked to publish this bundle. Until the record said so, the only difference between a rehearsal and a published review was which folder it sat in, and a folder can be copied.

id.$comment: The bundle's path inside this repository, or its slug and route when it was written elsewhere. Never an absolute path, for the same reason as generator.run.directory.

allOf.$comment: The hosted panel's obligations, unchanged. Every record already published as version 2 still has to satisfy exactly this list.

then.$comment: Ajv strict mode asks that a required name also appear in this subschema's own properties. The real constraints for each one live in the top-level properties block, so these are deliberately empty.

allOf.$comment: A plugin run has no per-stage model split, no panel of five, no debate and no dollar cost, so it is not asked for them. What it must carry instead is the generator block: the code, the plugin, the agents, the transport and the human attestation that stand in for the hosted pipeline's accounting.

model.$comment: Refused outright rather than merely left out of the required list. Every version 2 record carries a single model id, and a reader of this file should not have to infer that a plugin run must not: the plugin pins a model per agent file, so one id at the top would describe a panel that did not sit. An empty not matches nothing, so a record carrying this key cannot validate.

models.$comment: The model each agent slot ran on, keyed by slot. At least one entry, because a record naming no model does not say what wrote the review, and the site reads exactly this field when it says what produced each report.

panel.$comment: Empty on a plugin run. The hosted panel's rows carried per-referee scores and dollar costs that this route does not produce. The equivalent record is generator.agents, which says what each slot was and what it delivered.

total_cost_usd.$comment: A subscription run has no per-review dollar figure. Null says so; a zero would read as a measured free run.
